newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's banking activity up in October.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's banking activity up in October.

text.p: The consolidated balance sheet of Lebanon's commercial banks registered a monthly rise of 4.26 percent in October to 34,775 billion Lebanese pounds, the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly bulletin.
Total deposits in foreign currencies and Lebanese pounds rose 5.06 percent to 29,062 billion pounds from 27,663 billion in September, it said.
Lebanese pound deposits grew 7.52 percent to 12,541 billion pounds from 11,664 billion a month earlier.
Deposits in foreign currencies grew 3.43 percent to $10.618 billion in October from $10.266 billion in September, the Bank added.
Dollarisation of bank deposits dropped to 56.85 percent from September's 57.84 percent. The dollarisation rate stood at 65.63 percent at the end of October 1995.
Loans and credits to the private sector rose 1.91 percent in October over September, increasing to 12,183 billion pounds.
Credits in Lebanese pounds rose 0.47 percent in October to 1,539 billion pounds.
Credits in foreign currencies rose 2.29 percent to $6.841 billion from $6.687 billion a month earlier.
Dollarisation of credits rose to 87.36 percent from 87.11 percent at the end of September, the Bank said.
